_comment: THE cross-language slash word. A slash word is what the Emacs composer
marks while it is typed (lisp/command-completion.el) and what the webapp
marks in a drawn user prompt (webapp/src/feed/rows/known-commands.ts),
when its name is a known command. The two are one rule in two languages:
the webapp reads this file as its rule's punctuation, and the elisp test
asserts its own constants against it and runs every case below, which is
the only mechanism that makes a divergence between the two fail loudly
THE RULE. A slash word lies in a run of non-whitespace. It begins with
'/' at the run's start or after the run's leading 'opening' punctuation,
and ends at the run's end less its trailing 'closing' punctuation, never
before the slash's next character. Its name is the word less its slash.
Each case is a text, the command names known, and the words marked, in
